Subject: Draft — Light Up a Life 2026

Hilary asked on the page this week whether we would be doing the tree again. Yes, Hilary, we are — and it would be lovely to see you and your sister. I’m so glad that having your mum’s name on last year’s tree meant so much.

Our Light Up a Life memory tags will be in the shop from Monday 16 November, with a suggested donation of £3. You are welcome to write your tag here, or there will be envelopes on the counter if you would rather take it home and write it in your own time. The tree itself will go into the window on Saturday 21 November.

We shall switch the lights on at 4pm on Saturday 28 November. The Gildencroft Primary choir are kindly coming back to sing three or four carols for us, and Doreen is doing her mince pies again. Do wrap up warm and come along if you can.

All the names on this year’s tags will be read out at the hospice remembrance service on Sunday 13 December at 3pm, in the day centre. You do not have to attend the service for your person’s name to be read. Come if you would like to, but please don’t feel that you must.

This November is seven years since my husband Ray died at the hospice. The first year I hung his tag, I could hardly write his name. Now I write it at the shop counter, with the same pen, while the ordinary business of the day goes on around me. It still isn’t easy, but it has become a moment in the year that I am grateful for. I mention it because I know how difficult that first tag can be. You can take all the time you need.

The tree is for anyone who is grieving, not only hospice families. There is no required connection to the hospice or to the bookshop, and no right way to remember somebody. And if you don’t want to write a tag at all, but would just like to come in and stand by the tree for a few minutes, please do. There is no need to buy anything, explain yourself or make conversation. You will be welcome simply to be there.

Last year the tree carried 412 names. Thank you to everyone who trusted us with one, to those who stood in the cold for the switch-on, and to everyone who stopped quietly by the window. Every name mattered to somebody, and we don’t take that trust lightly.

Thank you, as always, for remembering with us.

Jean
